question: Which Grand Slam tournament was played between 17 to 30 January 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australian Open.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Australian Open was held from 17 to 30 January 2022 at Melbourne Park, Melbourne, Australia. (ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन — जनवरी 2022)

 

• It is the first Grand Slam of the tennis calendar year, held annually in Melbourne since 1905 (originally the Australasian Championships).

 

• The men's singles title in 2022 was won by Rafael Nadal, completing a remarkable comeback from two sets down against Daniil Medvedev, while the women's singles title was won by Ashleigh Barty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The French Open (Roland Garros) is played on clay courts in Paris in May-June; Wimbledon is played on grass in London in June-July; the US Open is played on hard courts in New York in August-September.

 

• Together with the Australian Open, these four tournaments make up tennis's four Grand Slam events.

 

NOTE

 

• French Open (Option 1): Held in May-June at Roland Garros, Paris, on clay courts.

 

• Wimbledon open (Option 2): Held in June-July at the All England Club, London, on grass courts; it is the oldest Grand Slam, first held in 1877.

 

• US Open (Option 4): Held in August-September at Flushing Meadows, New York, on hard courts.

question: Why is PC Mahalanobis’ name talked about in the context of Five-Year Plans?
option_1: He was the chairman of the Planning Commission.
option_2: He established the Institute of Economic Growth.
option_3: He conceptualised the framework for the Second Five-Year Plan.
option_4: He was the finance minister during the First Five-Year Plan period.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He conceptualised the framework for the Second Five-Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, an eminent statistician, formulated the Mahalanobis model, the statistical-economic framework behind India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), which emphasised rapid industrialisation with a focus on heavy and basic industries. (पीसी महालनोबिस — द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• He founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata in 1931 and pioneered the use of statistics in economic planning in India.

 

• He served as a key member and statistical adviser to the Planning Commission, playing a central role in shaping India's planning strategy, though he was not its chairman.

 

• He is honoured as the "Father of Indian Statistics"; National Statistics Day is celebrated every year on his birthday, 29 June.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56), based on the Harrod-Domar model, focused on agriculture and irrigation.

 

• Mahalanobis also established the National Sample Survey (NSS) in 1950 for large-scale socio-economic data collection.

 

NOTE

 

• Chairman of Planning Commission (Option 1): The Prime Minister was the ex-officio Chairman of the (erstwhile) Planning Commission; Mahalanobis was a member/statistical adviser, not the chairman.

 

• Institute of Economic Growth (Option 2): This institute was established later, in 1958, by economist K.N. Raj, not Mahalanobis.

 

• Finance minister during First Plan (Option 4): Mahalanobis was never the finance minister; he served as a statistician-economist adviser to the government.

question: Which from the following is a phylum of animals found in fresh water ponds, lakes and swamps provides setae or parapodia for locomotion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annelida.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Phylum Annelida (segmented worms) includes species found in fresh water ponds, lakes and swamps; many possess setae (chitinous bristles) for locomotion, while polychaete annelids bear paired fleshy projections called parapodia. (एनेलिडा संघ — सीटी/पैरापोडिया द्वारा गमन)

 

• Common examples include earthworms and aquatic oligochaetes (which use setae), and marine/aquatic polychaetes such as Nereis (which use parapodia) for crawling and swimming.

 

• Annelids are coelomate, have a closed circulatory system, and show metameric (segmented) body organisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phylum Ctenophora (comb jellies) are marine, radially symmetric animals that move using rows of cilia called "combs", not setae or parapodia.

 

• Phylum Porifera (sponges) are sessile, non-motile filter feeders that lack any locomotory organs like setae or parapodia.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctenophora (Option 1): Marine comb jellies that use ciliary "combs" for locomotion, not setae/parapodia.

 

• Porifera (Option 2): Sponges are sessile filter-feeding animals with no locomotory structures.

 

• Platyhelminthes (Option 4): Flatworms (e.g., Planaria, tapeworms) move by cilia or muscular gliding, not by setae or parapodia.

question: Which autonomous body was operationalised under the Ministry of Surface Transport in 1995?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was constituted under the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988, but was made operational only from 15 February 1995, under the (then) Ministry of Surface Transport. (एनएचएआई — 1995 में परिचालन में आया)

 

• NHAI is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways in India, including flagship programmes like the Golden Quadrilateral and Bharatmala Pariyojana.

 

• Its headquarters is located in New Delhi, and it currently functions under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Surface Transport was later reorganised into the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and the Ministry of Shipping (now Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways).

 

• NHAI awards highway projects through models such as BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer), EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) and HAM (Hybrid Annuity Model).

 

NOTE

 

• BRO (Option 1): Established in 1960 under the Ministry of Defence, responsible for road infrastructure in border and strategic areas.

 

• CRIS (Option 2): Established in 1986 under the Ministry of Railways, handles information technology systems for Indian Railways.

 

• IWAI (Option 3): Established in 1986 under the Ministry of Shipping, regulates and develops inland waterways for navigation.

question: The slogan of which census of India was ‘Our Census, Our Future’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2011.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The slogan/motto of the Census of India 2011, the 15th Indian census, was "Our Census, Our Future". (जनगणना 2011 — हमारी जनगणना, हमारा भविष्य)

 

• Census 2011 was conducted in two phases — house-listing (April-September 2010) and population enumeration (February 2011) — by the Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

• As per Census 2011, India's population was about 121.09 crore, with a sex ratio of 943 females per 1000 males and a literacy rate of 74.04%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Census of India has been conducted every 10 years since 1872, with the first synchronous, all-India census held in 1881.

 

• The Census Commissioner for the 2011 Census was C. Chandramouli.

 

NOTE

 

• 1981, 2001 and 1991 (Options 1, 3 and 4): "Our Census, Our Future" was specifically the slogan for the 2011 Census, not for these earlier census years.

question: Micro credit or micro finance is a novel approach to bank with poor. In this approach bank credit is extended to the poor through _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is self-help groups.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Microcredit/microfinance is a novel approach in which banks extend small amounts of credit to the poor (who typically lack collateral) through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) — small, voluntary groups, usually of women, who pool savings and jointly access credit. (सूक्ष्म ऋण — स्वयं सहायता समूह)

 

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP), launched by NABARD in 1992, links SHGs to the formal banking system and is considered the world's largest microfinance programme.

 

• Microfinance through SHGs aims at the financial inclusion of economically weaker sections who are otherwise excluded from formal banking channels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), established in 1982, is the apex institution promoting rural and agricultural credit in India.

 

• Prominent microfinance institutions/models in India include SEWA Bank, Bandhan, and various RBI-regulated NBFC-MFIs.

 

NOTE

 

• Co-operative credit societies (Option 1): These are separate, formally structured cooperative credit institutions, distinct from the SHG-based microcredit model.

 

• RBI (Option 2): The Reserve Bank of India is the banking sector regulator; it does not itself extend microcredit directly to the poor.

 

• Anganwadees (Option 4): Anganwadis are child-care and nutrition centres under the ICDS scheme, unrelated to credit delivery.

question: Which state ranks first with a total length of 31.2 thousand km of rivers and canals, which is about 17% of the total length of rivers and canals in the country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uttar Pradesh ranks first among Indian states with a total length of about 31.2 thousand km of rivers and canals, roughly 17% of the country's total length of rivers and canals. (उत्तर प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक नदी-नहर लंबाई)

 

• UP is drained by major rivers such as the Ganga, Yamuna, Ghaghara and Gomti, and has an extensive network of irrigation canals fed by them, such as the Upper Ganga Canal and Sharda Canal.

 

• This extensive river-canal network supports both irrigation for the state's large agricultural sector and the potential for inland water transport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's inland waterway network was significantly expanded under the National Waterways Act, 2016, which declared 111 additional inland waterways as National Waterways.

 

• The Ganga (National Waterway-1), connecting Haridwar to Haldia, passes through Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for a dense network of backwaters and canals (e.g., the West Coast Canal), but with a much smaller total length than Uttar Pradesh.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Has an extensive deltaic river network in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, but ranks below Uttar Pradesh in total river-canal length.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Has significant river systems (Narmada, Chambal) but a smaller river-canal network than Uttar Pradesh.

question: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was incorporated in the year _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1967.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was incorporated on 9 November 1967 as a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. (हिंदुस्तान कॉपर लिमिटेड — स्थापना 1967)

 

• HCL is India's only vertically integrated copper-producing company, engaged in the exploration, mining, beneficiation, smelting and refining of copper.

 

• It operates mines and plants across Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Gujarat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• HCL holds Mini Ratna Category-I status among central public sector enterprises.

 

• Its registered office is located in Kolkata.

 

NOTE

 

• 1963, 1981 and 1972 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are not the correct incorporation year — HCL was incorporated in 1967.

question: Vajira Chitrasena of Sri Lanka was conferred the Padma Shri award 2020 for which of the following?
option_1: Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical dance
option_2: Enriching India- Sri Lanka ties through education
option_3: Enriching India- Sri Lanka ties through social work
option_4: Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical music
solution_text:
The correct answer is Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vajira Chitrasena, a veteran Sri Lankan dancer, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2020 by the Government of India for "Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical dance". (वजिरा चित्रसेना — पद्म श्री 2020, भारतीय शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• She trained in Bharatanatyam and is regarded as a pioneer of modern Sri Lankan (Kandyan) dance, blending Indian classical dance traditions with indigenous Sri Lankan dance forms.

 

• Along with her husband, Chitrasena, she co-founded the Chitrasena Dance Company, a leading dance institution in Sri Lanka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (26 January), in three categories — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

 

• Vajira Chitrasena is one of the very few foreign nationals honoured with a Padma award for services to Indian art and culture abroad.

 

NOTE

 

• Education (Option 2): Her recognised contribution was to classical dance, not education.

 

• Social work (Option 3): She was honoured for her contribution to dance, not social work.

 

• Indian classical music (Option 4): Her contribution was to dance, not music.

question: Which pioneer scientist used radio waves to transmit signals over distances of several kilometres in the 1890s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guglielmo Marconi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guglielmo Marconi, an Italian inventor, pioneered long-distance radio (wireless telegraphy) transmission, successfully sending signals over several kilometres in the 1890s, and later achieved the first transatlantic wireless transmission in 1901. (गुग्लिएल्मो मार्कोनी — रेडियो तरंगों के अग्रदूत)

 

• He shared the Nobel Prize in Physics, 1909 with Karl Ferdinand Braun for contributions to the development of wireless telegraphy.

 

• His work built on the electromagnetic wave theory of James Clerk Maxwell and the experimental demonstrations of Heinrich Hertz.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, Jagadish Chandra Bose independently demonstrated wireless signalling using microwaves around the same period (1895).

 

• Marconi founded the Marconi Company, a pioneering wireless telegraph and radio communications firm.

 

NOTE

 

• Michael Faraday (Option 1): Known for discoveries in electromagnetic induction, not for pioneering radio-wave transmission.

 

• Paul Langevin (Option 2): A French physicist known for work on magnetism and the development of sonar (ultrasound), not long-distance radio transmission.

 

• Pierre Weiss (Option 4): A French physicist known for the domain theory of ferromagnetism, unrelated to radio-wave transmission.

question: "India House", a revolutionary organisation, was established by Shyamji Krishna Varma in _________ for the spread of Indian Nationalism.
solution_text:
The correct answer is London.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "India House", a hostel and revolutionary organisation for Indian students, was established by Shyamji Krishna Varma in London (Highgate) in 1905, to promote Indian nationalism and anti-colonial activity among Indian students in Britain. (इंडिया हाउस — लंदन, श्यामजी कृष्ण वर्मा)

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma also founded the Indian Home Rule Society and the newspaper "The Indian Sociologist" in London.

 

• India House became a hub for revolutionaries such as Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, Madan Lal Dhingra and V.V.S. Aiyar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madan Lal Dhingra, associated with India House, assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909.

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma also instituted scholarships to send Indian students abroad for higher studies.

 

NOTE

 

• Singapore, San Francisco and Paris (Options 1, 3 and 4): India House was established in London, not in these cities — though Paris was later a base for other Indian revolutionaries such as Madame Bhikaji Cama.

question: In December 2022, India’s Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has recommended the federal government to introduce a pension scheme like UK pension scheme for the country’s _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is gig workers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In December 2022, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) recommended that the central government introduce a pension scheme, on the lines of the UK's pension scheme, for the country's gig workers — workers in the platform/gig economy, such as app-based delivery and ride-hailing workers. (पीएफआरडीए — गिग वर्कर्स हेतु पेंशन योजना)

 

• The proposal envisaged auto-enrolment of gig workers into a pension scheme with contributions from aggregator platforms, broadly modelled on the UK's National Employment Savings Trust (NEST) approach.

 

• PFRDA is the statutory regulator for pension funds in India, established under the PFRDA Act, 2013, and it also administers the National Pension System (NPS).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Code on Social Security, 2020 also provides for extending social security benefits, including pension, to gig and platform workers in India.

 

• PFRDA has subsequently explored initiatives to allow gig workers to voluntarily subscribe to the NPS with low minimum contributions.

 

NOTE

 

• Paramedics, farmers and textile workers (Options 1, 2 and 4): PFRDA's December 2022 recommendation specifically targeted gig workers, not these other occupational groups.

question: The Prime Minister Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana was announced in which year’s Union Budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021-22.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana (PMASBY) was announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in the Union Budget 2021-22, as a new centrally sponsored scheme to strengthen India's healthcare infrastructure. (आत्मनिर्भर स्वस्थ भारत योजना — बजट 2021-22)

 

• It was formally launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 October 2021, with an outlay of about ₹64,180 crore over six years, in addition to the National Health Mission.

 

• The scheme aims to develop the capacities of primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare systems and to strengthen existing, as well as create new, national institutions to detect and treat emerging diseases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme is implemented alongside the National Health Mission (NHM) and complements the Ayushman Bharat programme.

 

• Key components include Integrated District Public Health Laboratories and Critical Care Hospital Blocks in all districts.

 

NOTE

 

• 2018-19, 2020-21 and 2019-20 (Options 1, 3 and 4): PMASBY was announced in the Union Budget 2021-22, in the backdrop of the COVID-19 pandemic, not in any of these earlier budgets.

question: Which of the following states organises ‘Lokrang’, a five-day festival, beginning every year on 26 January?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Lokrang" is a five-day cultural festival organised by the Madhya Pradesh Department of Culture, held every year beginning 26 January (Republic Day) at Bhopal. (लोकरंग महोत्सव — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The festival showcases the folk and tribal art, dance and music traditions of Madhya Pradesh, bringing together artists from across the state on a common platform.

 

• It is organised annually to celebrate and preserve the state's rich folk cultural heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh also hosts other notable cultural events such as the Khajuraho Dance Festival and the Tansen Music Festival.

 

• The state is known for tribal art forms such as Gond and Bhil paintings.

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh (Options 1, 2 and 4): "Lokrang" is specifically a Madhya Pradesh state festival, not associated with these states.

question: The art of decoration, called Pietra dura became popular during whose reign?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pietra dura (Italian for "hard stone"), an inlay art form using cut and polished coloured stones to create images and patterns on marble, became popular in India during the reign of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan (1628-1658). (पित्रा ड्यूरा — शाहजहाँ का शासनकाल)

 

• It is most famously seen in the decoration of the Taj Mahal at Agra, built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, and in the Diwan-i-Khas at the Red Fort, Delhi.

 

• The technique used semi-precious stones such as lapis lazuli, jade, turquoise and carnelian, inlaid into white marble in intricate floral and geometric designs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pietra dura originated in Italy (Florence) and reached India through Mughal court contacts with European artisans.

 

• Shah Jahan's reign is considered the golden age of Mughal architecture, also seeing the construction of the Jama Masjid and the Red Fort.

 

NOTE

 

• Jahangir (Option 1): Known for patronage of Mughal painting and gardens, not for popularising pietra dura.

 

• Sher Shah Suri (Option 2): A ruler of the Suri dynasty (pre-Mughal interregnum), known for the Grand Trunk Road and his tomb at Sasaram, unrelated to pietra dura.

 

• Akbar (Option 4): Known for Mughal architecture such as Fatehpur Sikri, but pietra dura became prominent later, under Shah Jahan.

question: In 1908, _________ and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage that was occupied, they believed, by Kingsford, the unpopular judge of Muzzafarpur.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khudiram Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1908, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, believing it carried the unpopular British judge Kingsford; the bomb instead killed two British women (Mrs. and Miss Kennedy) travelling in a similar carriage. (खुदीराम बोस — मुजफ्फरपुर बम कांड 1908)

 

• Khudiram Bose was arrested, tried and executed by hanging on 11 August 1908, at the age of 18, becoming one of the youngest martyrs of the Indian freedom struggle.

 

• Prafulla Chaki shot himself to avoid capture by the police.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Muzaffarpur bombing was linked to the revolutionary activities of groups associated with the Anushilan Samiti in Bengal.

 

• Khudiram Bose is commemorated across India, including through institutions and memorials named after him.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 1): A later revolutionary (1907-1931), known for the Central Assembly bombing (1929) and the Saunders murder case, not the 1908 Muzaffarpur incident.

 

• Rajguru (Option 3): Associated with Bhagat Singh in the 1928 assassination of J.P. Saunders, not the 1908 Muzaffarpur bombing.

 

• Jaitndranath Bose (Option 4): Not associated with the 1908 Muzaffarpur bomb incident; it was Prafulla Chaki, not Jaitndranath Bose, who accompanied Khudiram Bose.

question: Jamda folk dance is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jamda folk dance is associated with the state of Jharkhand, performed by tribal communities as part of their cultural and festive traditions. (जामदा नृत्य — झारखंड)

 

• Jharkhand has a rich tradition of tribal folk dances performed during festivals and social occasions, reflecting the culture of communities such as the Santhal, Oraon and Munda.

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Jharkhand include Jhumair, Domkach, Paika and Chhau.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chhau dance of Jharkhand (along with its Odisha and West Bengal variants) is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar as a separate state on 15 November 2000.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Known for folk dances such as Bihu, not Jamda.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for folk dances such as Lavani and Dhangari Gaja, not Jamda.

 

• Manipur (Option 3): Known for classical Manipuri dance and folk forms such as Thang-Ta, not Jamda.

question: The capital of Vajji Mahajanapada was _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaishali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vaishali (in present-day Bihar) was the capital of the Vajji (Vrijji) Mahajanapada, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of ancient India. (वैशाली — वज्जि महाजनपद की राजधानी)

 

• The Vajji Mahajanapada was a confederacy/republic (gana-sangha) of clans, including the Licchavis, considered one of the earliest examples of a republican form of government.

 

• Vaishali is also significant as the birthplace of Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, and as the site of the Second Buddhist Council.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The sixteen Mahajanapadas are described in early Buddhist texts such as the Anguttara Nikaya.

 

• Vaishali was visited several times by Gautam Buddha and is associated with important events in early Buddhism.

 

NOTE

 

• Pataliputra (Option 1): Capital of the Magadha Mahajanapada (later of the Mauryan and Gupta empires), not Vajji.

 

• Champa (Option 2): Capital of the Anga Mahajanapada, not Vajji.

 

• Koshala (Option 4): Capital of the Koshala Mahajanapada was Shravasti/Ayodhya, not related to Vajji.

question: In which year was the 1st winter edition of the Olympic Games organised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1924.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Winter Olympic Games were held in 1924 at Chamonix, France, originally named "International Winter Sports Week" and retroactively recognised by the IOC in 1926 as the first Winter Olympics. (शीतकालीन ओलंपिक — प्रथम संस्करण 1924, शामोनी)

 

• About 16 nations and around 258 athletes participated, competing in sports such as skiing, skating, ice hockey and bobsleigh.

 

• The Winter Olympics have since been held roughly every four years; from 1994 onward they alternate on a two-year cycle with the Summer Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1920 Summer Olympics were held in Antwerp, Belgium, and included some winter sports like figure skating and ice hockey before a separate Winter Olympics existed.

 

• India has not yet won a medal at the Winter Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 1926, 1920 and 1922 (Options 1, 2 and 3): The inaugural Winter Olympic Games were held in 1924, not in these years.

question:
Which of the following pair of compound – boiling point is correct?

I. Chloroform – 334K

II. Methane – 111K
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. The boiling point of chloroform (CHCl₃) is about 334 K (61.2°C), and the boiling point of methane (CH₄) is about 111 K (−162°C). (क्लोरोफॉर्म व मीथेन — क्वथनांक सही)

 

• Statement I is correct: Chloroform, a colourless liquid used as a solvent and historically as an anaesthetic, boils at approximately 334 K.

 

• Statement II is correct: Methane, the simplest hydrocarbon (alkane) and the main component of natural gas, has a very low boiling point of approximately 111 K because it is a small, non-polar molecule held together only by weak van der Waals forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Boiling point generally rises with increasing molecular weight and stronger intermolecular forces (e.g., hydrogen bonding, dipole-dipole interactions); methane, being a small non-polar molecule, has a far lower boiling point than chloroform.

 

• Chloroform is a trihalomethane and was once widely used as a general anaesthetic before safer alternatives were developed.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II (methane's boiling point) is also correct.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, because both statements are factually accurate.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement I (chloroform's boiling point) is also correct.

question: Who administers oath of office to the Vice President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The President of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 69 of the Constitution of India, the oath of office to the Vice-President of India is administered by the President of India (or a person appointed by the President in that behalf). (उपराष्ट्रपति शपथ — राष्ट्रपति द्वारा)

 

• In the oath, the Vice-President undertakes to "bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India" and to "faithfully discharge the duty upon which about to enter."

 

• The Vice-President of India is also the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, the oath of office to the President of India is administered by the Chief Justice of India (or, in their absence, the senior-most available judge of the Supreme Court), under Article 60.

 

• The Vice-President of India at the time of this exam was Jagdeep Dhankhar, who was sworn in on 11 August 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• The Prime Minister of India (Option 1): Does not administer the oath to the Vice-President.

 

• The Speaker of Lok Sabha (Option 2): Administers oaths in certain other contexts, not to the Vice-President.

 

• The Chief Justice of India (Option 4): Administers the oath to the President of India, not to the Vice-President.

question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed by the Parliament. This is pertaining to the state of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, passed by Parliament in December 2022, pertains to the state of Uttar Pradesh — it grants Scheduled Tribe status to the Gond community and its sub-castes (Dhuria, Nayak, Ojha, Pathari, Rajgond) in select districts of Uttar Pradesh where they were previously not so recognised. (अनुसूचित जनजाति आदेश द्वितीय संशोधन विधेयक 2022 — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• The Bill amended the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1967, as applicable to Uttar Pradesh, on the recommendation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

 

• This was one of three related Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes Order amendment bills passed during the Winter Session of Parliament, December 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related bill in the same session, the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Third Amendment) Bill, 2022, granted ST status to the Hattee community of the Trans-Giri area of Sirmaur district, Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Amendments to the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes lists require an Act of Parliament, as these lists are notified under Articles 341 and 342 of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Kerala (Options 1, 2 and 4): This particular Second Amendment Bill, 2022 pertained specifically to Uttar Pradesh, not to these states.

question: Who among the following personalities is associated with the musical instrument Mandolin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is U Srinivas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• U. Srinivas (Uppalapu Srinivas), popularly known as "Mandolin U. Srinivas," was a renowned Indian classical musician who pioneered adapting the Western mandolin to play Carnatic classical music. (मैंडोलिन श्रीनिवास — कर्नाटक संगीत)

 

• He began performing publicly from a very young age and became internationally acclaimed for his mandolin recitals, collaborating with artists across genres, including the fusion ensemble Remember Shakti.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri (1998) and later the Padma Bhushan (2010) for his outstanding contribution to Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• U. Srinivas passed away in 2014 at the young age of 45, but left a lasting legacy in popularising the mandolin as a classical Carnatic instrument.

 

• Other instruments and their associated maestros include the violin (Lalgudi Jayaraman, M.S. Gopalkrishnan), the Hawaiian slide guitar/"Mohan Veena" (Vishwa Mohan Bhatt), and the Hindustani slide guitar (Brij Bhushan Kabra).

 

NOTE

 

• Brij Bhushan Kabra (Option 1): Known as a pioneer of the Hindustani slide guitar, not the mandolin.

 

• Vishwa Mohan Bhat (Option 2): Known for adapting the Hawaiian guitar into the "Mohan Veena," not the mandolin.

 

• MS Gopalkrishnan (Option 4): A renowned Carnatic violinist, not associated with the mandolin.

question: Which of the following committees recommended for the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swaran Singh Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swaran Singh Committee, set up by the government in 1976, recommended the inclusion of a chapter on Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India. (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Based on its recommendations, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added a new Part IV-A to the Constitution, comprising Article 51A, which originally listed ten Fundamental Duties.

 

• An eleventh Fundamental Duty (the duty of parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to their child) was later added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Fundamental Duties are inspired by Article 57 of the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they are not directly enforceable through the courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarkaria Commission (Option 2): Set up in 1983 to examine and recommend on Centre-State relations, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Rajamannar Committee (Option 3): Set up by the Tamil Nadu government in 1969, also concerned with Centre-State relations, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (Option 4): Set up in 1957, recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, not Fundamental Duties.

question: Pepperonil, ethyl acetate, butyraldehyde and nitrate are some common adulterants used in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is ice cream.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pepperonil (piperonal), ethyl acetate, butyraldehyde and nitrate are common chemical adulterants used to fake or enhance the flavour of ice cream — for example, piperonal is used to imitate vanilla flavour, while ethyl acetate and butyraldehyde are used as artificial fruity flavouring agents. (आइसक्रीम में मिलावट — पिपेरोनल, एथिल एसीटेट)

 

• Such food adulteration is regulated and monitored under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), established under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

 

• Use of these unauthorised chemical adulterants in food products can pose health hazards and is a punishable offence under food safety laws.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common adulterants in other foods include sugar syrup/starch in honey, argemone oil in mustard oil, and metanil yellow in spices/pulses.

 

• FSSAI promotes the "Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test (DART)" booklet/kit to help consumers identify common food adulterants at home.

 

NOTE

 

• Honey (Option 1): Commonly adulterated with sugar syrup or starch, not with piperonal, ethyl acetate, butyraldehyde or nitrate.

 

• Oils (Option 3): Commonly adulterated with cheaper oils such as argemone oil, not with these specific chemicals.

 

• Spices (Option 4): Commonly adulterated with colours (e.g., metanil yellow, lead chromate) or foreign matter, not with these specific chemicals.
